answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as a quartz security deposit. Each stake functions as a bridge between digital identity and economic accountability. If an agent behaves maliciously, its umber ledger balance is slashed, imposing a prohibitive financial cost on attackers attempting to spawn multiple identities. This mechanism binds network influence to verifiable asset ownership, rendering the mass creation of fake agents unprofitable.
